title: Great Britain's Tennis Team Fought Hard but Lost to the Czech Republic
summary:
Imagine playing tennis for three whole hours — after not playing for six months because of an injury. That's what Sonay Kartal did for Great Britain in the Billie Jean King Cup.

The Billie Jean King Cup is a big team tennis competition. Great Britain was the underdog against the Czech Republic. All five Czech players were ranked higher than any British player.

Kartal returned from a lower back injury to face Marie Bouzkova. It was a marathon match. Kartal saved three match points and fought back, but Bouzkova won 7-6, 4-6, 6-4. The match lasted exactly three hours.

Next up was Katie Boulter, Britain's highest-ranked player. She faced Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova. Boulter lost 6-2, 7-6. That meant the Czech Republic won the tie.

Great Britain's captain, Anne Keothavong, was proud of her team. "I can't fault their efforts," she said. "The Czechs are the strongest team here. I'd be surprised if they don't go on to win the competition."

Kartal said the match gave her confidence for the rest of the season. "These events are my favourite, but they also sting the most," she said.

Great Britain's wait for a first title continues. The Czech Republic moves on to the semi-finals.
why_it_matters: It shows that you can be proud of your effort even when you lose, and that coming back from an injury takes real courage.

background_read: The Billie Jean King Cup (an international team competition for women's tennis, played a bit like a World Cup) is named after Billie Jean King, a famous American tennis champion who fought for women players to be treated fairly.
The Czech Republic (a country in central Europe) has a long history of producing very strong women tennis players.
In this competition, teams of players face each other in matches, and the team that wins more matches wins the whole 'tie' and moves on.
Article_Structure: WHO: Sonay Kartal, Katie Boulter, and captain Anne Keothavong for Great Britain; Marie Bouzkova and Linda Noskova for the Czech Republic
WHAT: Great Britain lost both matches and therefore lost the tie
WHERE: At the Billie Jean King Cup team tennis competition
WHY: Every Czech player was ranked higher than the British players, and Kartal was coming back from a back injury after six months away
